summary: A huge pre-Diwali rally meets its first sign of fatigue: early festive buying was sold into, leaving Monday to show whether foreign demand can outlast profit-taking and Gulf risk.

detail.leaders: Metals and pharma, where Tata Steel and Sun Pharma led the early Muhurat gains
detail.laggards: Infosys, IndiGo, Trent and L&T, which lagged from the start of the Muhurat session
detail.tone: Today's one-hour Muhurat session was a real but thin, ceremonial trade: it opened firmly, then gave back its gains to close slightly lower, ending a long run of Diwali-session gains. The next full session is Monday Nov 9; Tuesday Nov 10 is a holiday.
